subject.title: [Bug]: browser navigation-guard explicit hostname allowlist broken by SSRF loopback tightening (#100835)

question: Should browser navigation allowlisted hostnames be allowed to resolve to loopback after the trusted-host SSRF hardening, and which DNS-answer checks must remain enforced?
rationale: Both choices affect the SSRF trust boundary: restoring the old test behavior helps operator-declared browser exceptions, while keeping the hardening avoids reauthorizing non-localhost loopback rebinding.

options.title: Approve a scoped browser exception
options.body: Restore only the maintainer-approved loopback case for browser navigation allowlists while preserving metadata and link-local DNS-answer rejection.

options.title: Retire the loopback-alias contract
options.body: Keep the new trusted-host loopback hardening and update the browser navigation test/docs to require localhost, loopback literals, or explicit private-network opt-in.

options.title: Pause for broader SSRF design
options.body: Leave the issue and linked PR blocked until browser, CDP, provider, and shared SSRF allowlist semantics are decided together.

recommendation.title: Approve a scoped browser exception
recommendation.body: Restore only the maintainer-approved loopback case for browser navigation allowlists while preserving metadata and link-local DNS-answer rejection.

likelyOwner.reason: They opened the canonical issue and framed the exact SSRF/browser boundary decision that remains unresolved.
